items.claim: this pricing change raises revenue per order

cases.text: One: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 4 March; by 29 March revenue per order ran 6 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.
Two: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 5 March; by 30 March revenue per order ran 4 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.
Three: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 6 March; by 31 March revenue per order ran 7 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.
Four: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 7 March; by 28 March revenue per order ran 5 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.

items.passage:
A retail log records four product lines after a new pricing rule took effect.
One: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 4 March; by 29 March revenue per order ran 6 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.
Two: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 5 March; by 30 March revenue per order ran 4 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.
Premium stock's share of each store's shelf held level, matching the earlier period exactly, and every line was stocked straight from that shelf. Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and the new prices applied to all orders on the lines.
Three: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 6 March; by 31 March revenue per order ran 7 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.
Four: coffee at Harlow Street repriced 7 March; by 28 March revenue per order ran 5 percent above the same line a month earlier; lead Vasquez.
Each entry was transcribed to the regional ledger and countersigned by the district accounts clerk.
items.notes: Check that all four lines share one value on every dimension: store Harlow Street, category coffee, month March, region lead Vasquez. Closer is CHANGED fact + BLOCK scope: the premium share of the shelf did move, but every line came from a fixed year-round range, so the mix shift cannot reach these lines and the tail rules out everything else.

items.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the figures over the orders rung up at the new prices, and the clause beside it records that about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices. The claim is about revenue per order on the repriced lines, so the population is every order on those lines and the numbers describe roughly four fifths of it. Orders still ringing at the old list are the lower-value ones by construction, so an average built from new-price orders alone sits above the line's own figure, and the 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent gains are consistent with revenue per order across all orders holding flat. Every case is coffee at Harlow Street inside March under lead Vasquez, so the same excluded fifth sits under all four cases and no case in the log covers it.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Closer is CHANGED fact + REACH scope. The assortment shift works as a single confound precisely because the four lines share one store, one category and one month - four coffee lines on one shelf in March cannot be told apart from that shelf. Across the family CHANGED appears once in a TRUE item and once in a FALSE item, and so does REACH, so no single clause is a label marker.
